title: ABC-FHE: A Resource-Efficient Accelerator Enabling Bootstrappable Parameters for Client-Side Fully Homomorphic Encryption
problem: Client-side Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) computations remain a bottleneck, particularly under bootstrappable parameter configurations involving encoding, encryption, decoding, and decryption for large parameters, requiring 10,000-fold more computation than plaintext processing.
method: ABC-FHE employs a streaming architecture with a reconfigurable Fourier engine capable of switching between NTT (Number-Theoretic Transform) and FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) modes. It includes an on-chip pseudo-random number generator and unified on-the-fly twiddle factor generator to reduce memory demands, with optimized task scheduling to enhance CKKS client-side processing, reducing off-chip memory access.

title: QECC-Synth: A Layout Synthesizer for Quantum Error Correction Codes on Sparse Architectures
problem: Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes require dense qubit connectivity that does not match the sparse qubit coupling graphs of current hardware architectures, and existing QEC circuit compilation approaches either underutilize QEC circuit structure or rely on manual, architecture-specific designs that do not generalize.
method: QECC-Synth is an automated compiler that uses the ancilla bridge technique—inserting ancilla qubits to implement long-range interactions over sparse coupling graphs—and systematically classifies the design space flexibilities of this technique. It then formulates the layout synthesis problem as a MaxSAT optimization problem over these flexibility dimensions, finding globally near-optimal ancilla placement and routing for a given QEC code and hardware architecture. This approach is architecture-agnostic and handles diverse QEC codes (e.g., surface code, color code) without manual redesign.

title: Generative Model Based Standard Cell Timing Library Characterization
problem: Accurate cell timing characterization across PVT corners is essential for timing verification, but conventional SPICE simulation becomes prohibitively expensive as corner count explodes in modern designs, limiting scalability.
method: Uses a hybrid generative adversarial network (GAN) and autoencoder to learn and generalize timing arcs and corners, treating characterization as a generative modeling problem; the model learns distributions across timing arcs enabling efficient generation of corner timing data without expensive SPICE simulations.

title: Early Bug Detector - A Verification Methodology for DFD-SoC RTL Parameters
problem: Design for Debug (DFD) has become a crucial feature in complex System-on-Chips (SoCs) to provide effective debugging capabilities
method: Design for Debug (DFD) has become a crucial feature in complex System-on-Chips (SoCs) to provide effective debugging capabilities

title: WindServe: Efficient Phase-Disaggregated LLM Serving with Stream-based Dynamic Scheduling
problem: Phase-disaggregated LLM serving systems that separate compute-bound prefill from memory-bandwidth-bound decoding still suffer from coarse-grained static scheduling that leaves prefill compute overloaded while decoding resources sit idle, creating queuing delays and underutilization. KV cache transfers between disaggregated phases introduce additional scheduling overhead that further degrades latency SLOs.
method: WindServe implements a global scheduler that continuously monitors compute and memory resource usage across prefill and decoding pools and dynamically orchestrates cross-phase job assignments to reduce queuing delay and KV-cache swapping overhead. A stall-free rescheduling strategy saturates memory resources while minimizing overhead from KV cache transfers between phases. A stream-based pipeline mitigates interference between prefill and decoding jobs running concurrently by separating their execution streams and managing dependencies asynchronously.

title: A 6.78MHz Single-Stage Regulating Rectifier with Dual Outputs Simultaneously Charged in a Half Cycle Achieving 92.2% Efficiency and 131mW Output Power
problem: Wireless power transfer (WPT) to implanted biomedical devices requires efficient power conditioning, and implants often need multiple output voltages (e.g., low voltage for biopotential recording, high voltage for neurostimulation) with different performance requirements (stability vs. bandwidth). Single-output rectifiers cannot simultaneously meet these conflicting demands.
method: Single-stage regulating rectifier with dual simultaneous outputs per half-cycle at 6.78MHz switching frequency. The architecture achieves independent regulation of two output voltages: low stable voltage (V_OUT2) for recording front-end and high-bandwidth voltage (V_OUT1) for stimulation back-end, within a single rectifier stage rather than cascading multiple stages.

title: 34.6 A 47.3-to-58.4GHz Differential Quasi-Class-E Colpitts Oscillator Achieving 198.8dBc/Hz FoMT
problem: Millimeter-wave communication systems (5G, satellite) require local-oscillation signals with exceptionally high spectral purity (low phase noise and spurs). Traditional mm-wave VCOs suffer limited performance; harmonic-extraction approaches require power-hungry amplification stages; multi-core coupling topologies achieve only 190–191dB FoM(T), falling 5–10dB short of low-frequency counterparts.
method: A quasi-class-E Colpitts (QCEC) oscillator with transformer-based two-port resonance enables high-frequency fundamental oscillation, waveform shaping for efficiency, and integrated phase-noise suppression. Implemented in 40nm CMOS with 47.3–58.4GHz tuning range, achieving -124.9 to -119.8dBc/Hz phase noise at 10MHz offset.

title: A Modular, Responsive, and Accessible HPC Dashboard Built upon Open OnDemand
problem: HPC systems have high barriers to entry for non-expert users due to reliance on command-line tools; growing user community requires more accessible interfaces.
method: Modern web-based dashboard built on Open OnDemand framework with redesigned functional pages: announcements, system status, job information, resource usage.

title: Design and Implementation of a Custom Hardware Accelerator for SZx Compression in Chipyard
problem: Data movement is a dominant bottleneck in modern computing. Scientific detectors generate unprecedented data volumes (X-ray terabytes/sec, HEP petabytes/sec). Streaming compression with hardware acceleration can reduce data movement overhead.
method: Design and implement custom hardware accelerator for SZx (streaming compression) using modern HDLs in Chipyard. Multi-stage state machine, parallel element processing, optimized data transfers. Compare with software baseline.

title: IntraFuzz: Coverage-Guided Intra-Enclave Fuzzing for Intel SGX Applications
problem: Intel SGX applications are vulnerable to intra-enclave software vulnerabilities; existing automated bug-finding methods focus on fuzzing enclave boundaries in simulated environments, missing vulnerabilities in actual hardware-protected enclaves.
method: IntraFuzz is the first system enabling efficient coverage-guided fuzzing of SGX applications inside actual hardware-protected Intel SGX enclaves. The system integrates with SGX runtime to instrument enclave code and collect coverage feedback during fuzzing, enabling hardware-based vulnerability detection on real SGX platforms.

title: ConnectX-8 SuperNIC
problem: AI data centers require ultra-high-speed networking for distributed training and inference; ConnectX-8 SuperNIC addresses bottlenecks in Ethernet switching and packet processing at scale.
method: ConnectX-8 integrates programmable packet processing, in-network computing (INC) for collective operations, advanced congestion control, and high-speed switching fabric to deliver ultra-low-latency, high-throughput networking optimized for AI workloads.

title: 9.10 A 93%-Peak-Efficiency Battery-Input 12-to-36V-Output Inductor-in-the-Middle Hybrid Boost Converter with Continuous Input and Output Currents and Fast Transient with No RHP Zero
problem: Conventional boost converters face challenges in high voltage conversion ratios with very short turn-on pulses, significant voltage stress on inductors and transistors, and inherent right-half-plane zero that limits transient response speed.
method: Proposes a hybrid inductor-in-the-middle topology that reduces voltage stress on components, mitigates the RHP zero issue, and enables faster transient response while maintaining continuous input and output currents for improved efficiency and reliability.

title: An Algorithm-Hardware Co-design Based on Revised Microscaling Format Quantization for Accelerating Large Language Models
problem: Microscaling (MX) format offers promise as drop-in FP32 replacement but lacks practical hardware support; dominant low-precision LLM inference still relies on low-bit quantization, limiting scalability of MX format deployment.
method: Algorithm-hardware co-design with two levels: (1) RMFQ (Revised MX Format Quantization) introduces revised MX (RMX) format with novel group direction strategy for improved quantization; (2) RMFA (Revised MX Format Accelerator) implements RMX-adaptive hardware architecture and RMX encoding scheme optimized for low-bit operations.

title: Mosaic: Exploiting Instruction-Level Parallelism on Deep Learning Accelerators with iTex Tessellation
problem: Deep learning compilers use top-down tiling to map tensor computations homogeneously to a single type of hardware arithmetic unit (scalar, vector, or tensor), failing to exploit simultaneous use of all available compute units (scalar, vector, and tensor) in parallel. This leaves substantial instruction-level parallelism (ILP) on CPUs and GPUs unexploited, especially when computations can be decomposed into mixed instruction types.
method: Mosaic introduces iTex (instruction-level texture) tessellation: a compiler technique that decomposes a tensor computation task into heterogeneous sub-tiles assigned to different hardware arithmetic units (scalar, vector, tensor) simultaneously. The tessellation partitions the iteration space of a tensor operation such that different sub-regions are mapped to the most appropriate unit type, and the schedule coordinates their concurrent execution. A compiler pass analyzes operation shapes and hardware unit capabilities to determine the optimal tessellation, then generates mixed-instruction kernel code that overlaps scalar, vector, and tensor unit execution within a single kernel.

title: BoolE: Exact Symbolic Reasoning via Boolean Equality Saturation
problem: Boolean symbolic reasoning on gate-level netlists for verification and synthesis struggles to accurately identify multi-input, multi-output structures (e.g., full adders). Conventional approaches using structural hashing are sensitive to structural modifications from technology mapping and logic optimization.
method: BoolE applies equality saturation with domain-specific Boolean rewriting rules to gate-level netlists. A novel extraction algorithm identifies and captures multi-input, multi-output high-level structures in the reconstructed e-graph, improving structural insight and computational efficiency.

title: Performance-Portable Symbolic Factorization through Common Graph Operations
problem: Symbolic factorization in sparse LU decomposition is essential for understanding sparsity patterns and fill-ins, but existing approaches rely on specialized graph algorithms that are difficult to port efficiently across diverse hardware.
method: Express edge-based and path-based symbolic factorization using common GraphBLAS operations. Investigate use of masks and elimination trees for optimization. Evaluate on multi-core and many-core architectures for various sparse matrices.
